LESSON: WRITING 13.4.1 GUIDED WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.4: Writing 13.4.1 Guided writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 13.4.1 Guided writing, part of Strand 13 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three General.

Key inquiry question: Why should we write sentences correctly? 2.How do we form a paragraph?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 13.4.1 Guided writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination: The learner’s ability to come up with unique ideas is enhanced as they use the five steps of the

writing process to write a short paragraph about the theme.

Values:
Responsibility: as the learner gains self-drive to practise writing using the five step writing process.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: Effective communication as the learner communicates ideas in paragraphs.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Writing skill is integral in all learning areas.

Suggested Learning Resources

Chart, Class readers, Adapted Course books, Flash cards, Recording devices e.g tablets, mobile phone, Dictionary, Internet, Audio-visual recordings,

Posters, Pictures and Photographs, Extracts from newspapers, magazines.
